messages:
lina: quick one — saw a few edge cases when we rebind streaming requests to a different upstream and the client has already consumed part of the stream. should the gateway try to extend the client deadline automatically or fail fast?

sanjay: big question: if we extend and retry upstream, how do we prevent duplicate side effects? idempotency tokens help but not every backend supports them. :thinking_face:

olga: proposal sketch: let the gateway advertise a short negotiated extension window via headers, e.g. `X-RW-Extendable-Deadline: 250ms` and a consumer offset token `X-RW-Consumer-Offset: <frames>` so upstream can resume from a known point or fast-forward using KV cache. if upstream can't resume, it returns 412 and gateway fallbacks.

michael: with that we also need metrics: `edge.deadline_extensions`, `edge.resume_success`, `edge.resume_fail_consumer_consumed` so product and SRE can see how often this happens. also add a trace tag for `resume_path=fastforward|restart|fail`.

lina: nice. fallback policy idea: only allow auto-extend if `consumer_offset` <= 1 frame or bytes < 8KB (configurable). otherwise gateway should return a resumable-error payload that clients can use to retry from scratch. keeps client-visible behavior predictable. :thumbsup:

olga: agreed. draft header semantics I was thinking of:
```
# sent by client->gateway (optional)
Prefer-Resume: safe-only | allow-extend
Idempotency-Token: <uuid>

# gateway->upstream when we plan to retry/resume
X-RW-Extendable-Deadline: 250ms
X-RW-Consumer-Offset: 1024
X-RW-Retry-Mode: resume|restart
```

sanjay: note: `safe-only` means gateway won't request an extension for requests marked as side-effectful unless we have Idempotency-Token. defaults to `safe-only`. also, if `Idempotency-Token` present, upstream should be allowed to dedupe.

michael: operational gotcha: we need to cap number of extensions per request and surface a consumer-visible error when we exceed budget. maybe `edge.resume_budget` header for tracing.

lina: agree. next steps: olga, can you write an RFC follow-up with the header semantics, state machine sketch, and a small test matrix (consumer offset cases, cache-miss, backend-no-idempotency)? I'll loop in platform-telemetry for metrics.

olga: yep, I'll put up a draft PR tomorrow and include unit tests for the streaming harness. will add examples for both chunked and framed transports.

dev-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/edge-proxy v2026.03.23 will include test harness for resume-scenarios. :robot_face:

sanjay: thanks — let's sync 1:1 after the RFC. also let's add a quick doc in console about how customers should set `Prefer-Resume`.

lina: thanks everyone — this should reduce noisy client errors for transient upstream retries while keeping side-effect safety conservative.
